about: D-SRC-73 (2026-10-27): what the helper answers when a folder it writes into cannot be used, and the sentence the shell shows for it. The helper's code and the model's sentence are joined by a NAME, so both sides run this file (rule 13): tests/test_local_refusals.py applies each `damage` in a scratch directory, runs the REAL helper as a subprocess with `argv` (HOME, the XDG folders and PATH in the scratch directory, so nothing of the user's is read and no mpv can start), and compares its stdout with `reply` exactly, with `{dir}` the damaged folder, `{fixtures}` tests/fixtures, `{cache}` a seeded cache folder and `{id}` its first channel; tests/Model.test.js maps `reply` through Model.parseHelperStatus and Model.statusReason and compares `reason`, with `{dir}` a path under a home directory, and checks that the reason names no path and that Model.failureFromHost puts no host after it. Damages: `folder-link` -- {dir} is a symbolic link to a name that does not exist; `folder-file` -- a regular file is at {dir}; `parent-0500` -- {dir} does not exist and its parent is mode 0500 (skipped when the tests run as root, who is not refused); `lock-dir` -- {dir} is a 0700 folder with a folder at the player's lock file name, `player.lock`. D-PLY-30 (2026-10-27) added the player cases: `player start|restart|stop` answer in their own reply shape, `folder_unusable` (R25c's sentence) for a runtime folder that is a link to nothing, and `runtime_unwritable` (which of the two, the error's words, no path) for a runtime folder that cannot be made or a lock file that cannot be opened.
